- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior), true outcome often lags or reverses; apply 1–2 day lag correction or cap peak at 2–3% above prior.  
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 3–5% gap), apply upward bias correction for next 3–5 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1 to -1), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 days post-sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” values, model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
